svg.aria-label: A hook event: 9 states and 19 changes, 13 fired by a clock and 6 by a fact. Each change is an arrow; its table follows.
svg.title: A hook event: 9 states and 19 changes, 13 fired by a clock and 6 by a fact. Each change is an arrow; its table follows.

g.title: HE1, (agent) to received, fired by a fact: the agent runs the hook command with the event on stdin

HE2, received to lost, fired by a clock: on Windows a hook whose parent (cmd.exe, PowerShell, the launcher) was killed by its agent ends itself, seen by a 1 s check Timers: A125. Fact that could fire it: A wait on the parent's process handle. It becomes a fact.

HE3, received to start state known, fired by a clock: the hook asks the daemon whether Rerail is on in the folder (2 s; on Windows after a 2 s proof), then reads the database itself Timers: A103 A104 A134. Fact that could fire it: The checkout's start rows in the database, read-only (or the kept answer of the last start or stop). It becomes a fact.
HE4, start state known to answered, fired by a fact: Rerail is not on in the folder: the hook answers {}

HE5, start state known to daemon found, fired by a clock: the hook reads daemon.json and probes the daemon (2 s), then probes again with what is left of 12 s from its arrival Timers: A101 A102. Fact that could fire it: An earlier event the daemon left untaken: a later hook journals its event and answers at once. It becomes a fact.
HE6, start state known to lost, fired by a fact: no daemon runs: the hook logs the lost event and starts one
HE7, daemon found to lost, fired by a clock: the daemon stayed silent past the hook's 12 s: the event is logged as lost Timers: A101 A102 D58. Fact that could fire it: As HE5. It becomes a fact.

HE8, daemon found to holds the session lock, fired by a clock: parallel hooks of one session take a lock file: retried every 10 ms up to 30 s, taken over from a holder silent 10 s; the holder touches it every 1 s Timers: A120 A121 A122 A123 D39. Fact that could fire it: An OS lock on the lock file: the system frees it when the holder ends; a waiter blocks on it in a worker thread. It becomes a fact.
HE9, holds the session lock to sent, fired by a fact: the hook posts the event to the engine socket
HE10, sent to answered, fired by a fact: the daemon answers with the event's deliveries

HE11, sent to answered, fired by a clock: the answer waits for bounded work: the session walk after a shell command (10 s cap), edit checks (1 s for hooks, 10 s for OMP and Pi), Merge Assist's note (1 s), each Git call (10 s) Timers: A402 A403 A404 A405 A407 A606 B040 B042 B200 D36. Fact that could fire it: Each wait ends on its work; the session walk can read only the paths the engine's change notices name. It a fact, one bound left.

HE12, sent to lost, fired by a clock: the hook gives up after 30 s of socket silence; the daemon goes on, holds the session's queue, and records the Stop's steers as delivered Timers: A115 A406. Fact that could fire it: The request's close in the daemon (an AbortSignal tied to it): a Stop whose hook left collects no steers and frees the queue. It becomes a fact.

HE13, answered to recorded, fired by a clock: the daemon writes the event on its JavaScript thread; another process's transaction makes it wait up to 5 s per statement Timers: B212 D7 D8 D11. Fact that could fire it: A writer thread for records, and long writes routed through the daemon, so the answering thread never waits on SQLite. It becomes a fact.

HE14, answered to recorded, fired by a clock: a delivered steer's receipt is written by the hook itself: two SQLite opens, 5 s busy timeout each Timers: A133. Fact that could fire it: The daemon records the receipt it already knows it sent. It becomes a fact.

HE15, answered to answered, fired by a clock: a session start reads the dashboard address, checkout scope and rule count (2 s each), and each delivered steer one more read Timers: A131 A132 B001 B044. Fact that could fire it: The daemon knows them when it answers the event: put them in the answer. It becomes a fact.

HE16, holds the session lock to answered, fired by a clock: on Windows the lock file's removal is retried for up to 5.5 s while a scanner holds it Timers: A124. Fact that could fire it: An OS lock needs no removal. It becomes a fact.
HE17, lost to recorded, fired by a fact: the lost event is written to the hook failure log (a rename retried 2 s on Windows; read back over 24 h)

HE18, received to answered, fired by a clock: an MCP tool call: a 2 s proof (Windows) and a 2 s /healthz on the first call, then up to 30 s for the relay Timers: A223 A224 A225. Fact that could fire it: One deadline per call from its arrival, each wait ending on its answer. It a fact, one bound left.

HE19, received to answered, fired by a clock: an event streamed by a host without hooks waits for the daemon up to 12 s Timers: A222. Fact that could fire it: The probe's answer already ends it; the clock bounds an event loop that never runs again. It stays.
